questions.boundary: The broker boundary between Redpanda and Apache Kafka. After the move, Catalog Management (catalog service and image service) produces and consumes on Kafka; every other service (tenant, product-query, category-query) stays on Redpanda. Traffic crosses the boundary in two places. tenant.tenant.events is produced on Redpanda by the tenant service and consumed by both moved services (inbound). catalog.product.events, catalog.category.events and catalog.attribute.events are produced on Kafka by the moved services and consumed by the query services on Redpanda (outbound). The image service's consumption of catalog.product.events stays inside the boundary, because both producers of that topic (catalog and image service) move.

Every TenantUpdated/TenantDeleted event produced on Redpanda must reach the catalog service on Kafka, under the same topic name, at the group's current position (not replayed from the start). TenantUpdated runs per-tenant DB migrations, so a missed event leaves a new store without a catalog database schema. TenantDeleted schedules tenant cleanup, so a replay could re-trigger cleanup.
candidates.ecommerce-category-query-service|catalog: AttributeUpdated events produced on Kafka must keep reaching Redpanda catalog.attribute.events. The category query service joins attribute master data at read time, so missing events drop or misname category filter attributes.
CategoryUpdated events produced on Kafka must keep reaching Redpanda catalog.category.events after offset 4, in order, so the category read model behind the storefront stays current.
candidates.ecommerce-image-service|tenant.tenant.ev: The same tenant event stream must reach the image service on Kafka at its current offset. TenantDeleted drives the registered S3 tenant cleaner, which deletes the tenant's image prefix, so the stream must arrive neither lost nor replayed from the beginning.
AttributeUpdated events from the catalog service on Kafka must keep reaching Redpanda catalog.attribute.events after offset 20. Product queries join master attribute views at read time and drop attributes whose master is missing, so lost attribute events silently remove or misname attributes on the storefront.

ProductUpdated/ProductDeleted from the catalog service and ProductImagePromoted from the image service, both now produced on Kafka, must keep arriving on Redpanda catalog.product.events. They must keep their per-key order within the partition and be appended after offset 120 so the group continues from where it is. This topic has two producers that both move, so no producer may remain on Redpanda for it, or the image service on Kafka would miss events. The storefront read model, including image URLs, depends on this stream.
